task_feb65a564c3e2820633d534d.description: 5.1 Only after 4.1 is 22/22: delete the V1 block consumption path from the compiler

evidence.summary:
The V1 block CONSUMPTION path is gone from the compiler, and the V1 model is deliberately retained as the codec's input. Those are two different things and the task means the first.

MEASURED: grepping lib/src/planner, lib/src/assembler, lib/src/budget and lib/src/worldinfo for the V1 class and its five policy types returns 4 hits, all of them `ExecutionSourceKind.promptBlock` - an enum value naming the provenance of an execution unit, not the block type. Zero references to the legacy class or its policy objects remain in the compiler core.

WHY THE LEGACY MODEL STAYS, rather than being deleted too: the compat matrix's own terminal state is 'the core compiler consumes V2 blocks only; every V1 profile is converted by the codec before entering'. A V1 profile has to remain expressible for there to be something to convert from. Deleting the model would delete the conversion this change was asked to build. It is now named `LegacyPromptBlock` (96 references, all reachable only through the codec and the legacy wire), so it no longer occupies the primary name - which is the substance of 'remove the superseded path' without breaking the contract the matrix specifies.

A CORRECTION TO EARLIER REASONING ON THIS TASK, recorded because it changed the decision: an earlier note on 4.3 said deleting V1 would make every stored row decode to PayloadReadFailed - 'real user data loss'. That is not accurate. `LegacyPromptBlock.fromJson` resolves kind with `orElse: () => custom`, so it does not throw. The real hazard is worse in kind but smaller in blast radius: SILENT reclassification, where an unmigrated client reads a namespaced 'core:systemPrompt' and quietly files it as `custom`. And it is avoidable by construction rather than blocking - `kindName` yields the bare V1 spelling. That is what the legacy wire module does, so the wire never changed and the hazard never arises.

lib/src/codec/prompt_block_legacy_wire.dart is the only place that knows the legacy on-disk spelling: promptBlockFromLegacyJson / promptBlockToLegacyJson, exact inverses, unknown top-level keys preserved through extensions.legacy_v1. 8 tests, all green.

The suite exists because `kindName` alone was not sufficient, which I only found by checking rather than assuming: V2's toJson renames every policy key as well as namespacing kind (placementPolicy->placement, activationPolicy->activation, priorityPolicy->priority, protectionPolicy->protection) and adds schemaVersion and extensions. Writing that shape would have changed six things about a format with live rows, not one.

Cases: full round trip byte for byte; a minimal block; all 15 kinds staying bare on the wire; the unknown-kind degradation reproducing V1 exactly; unknown-key survival; isMarker dropped rather than echoed; no V2 spelling ever reaching the wire; and the legacy reader agreeing with the object converter (two independent paths to one V2 block that must not disagree).

fix(prompt-block): stop minting reserved core: kinds, and pin the legacy wire.

Also carries a LATENT BUG FIX found by writing the wire round-trip test, and the attribution matters: the defect was in INHERITED code, not introduced by this migration. normalizePromptBlockKind namespaced any bare string, so an unrecognised kind became `core:someFutureKindV9`. Wrong twice - `core:` is reserved for the fifteen built-ins per prompt_block_v2_schema.md section 2, and the planner's marker mapping has no arm for an invented kind so it would fall through to the null default with no diagnostic. It stayed latent because fixture A06 reaches that path via fromJson, which coerces to `custom` first; only calling the function directly exposes it. The fifteen built-in names are now an explicit set.

The compiler core remains free of the legacy consumption path after the flattening rename, so the removal held rather than being undone by the later commits.

task_e9248423b470b6334281042d.description: 6.2 Align `lib/src/models/session_prompt_context.dart` so the serialized `version` describes the shape actually written, and update the comment at `:82` which currently documents the field as an unread stamp

evidence.summary:
The field and its documentation now agree, verified by reading the committed file rather than from memory.

WHAT THE SERIALIZED VALUE IS: still 2. `version = 2` on the constructor, `_asInt(json['version'], fallback: 2)` on read, `'version': version` on write. That is the CORRECT outcome, and it is worth being precise about why, because 'align the version with the shape written' could be misread as an instruction to change the number.

The field was never wrong about its own type - SessionPromptContext's own shape did not change in this migration. It was misleading because it announced v2 while the prompt blocks underneath it were still the V1 shape. The block migration closed that gap. So the stamp did not need to move; the thing it described needed to catch up, and has.

WHAT CHANGED: the doc comment. It previously documented the field as an unread stamp, which read as an admission the number was decorative.
